Appendix A.3
Orderings of Multi-Index Sets

Here some basic facts allowing one to better understand vectorization of tensors are presented.

A.3.1
Equivalent Characterization of Total Orders for Finite Sets

Let
X
be a finite set, and define
N\overset{\text{def}}{=}|X|
, the number of elements in
X
.

Then there is a one-to-one correspondence between total orders (orderings) on the set
X
and bijections
[N]\overset{\phi}{\to}X
, allowing one to consider the two notions equivalent.

Given a bijection
[N]\overset{\phi}{\to}X
, one can define a total order
\preceq
on
X
via

x_{1}\preceq x_{2}\iff\phi^{-1}(x_{1})\leq\phi^{-1}(x_{2})\text{ for all }x_{1},x_{2}\in X\,.

This is the total order generated by requiring the function
\phi
to be monotone, i.e. order-preserving.

Conversely, given a total order
\preceq
on
X
, one can define a bijection with
[N]
via the rule:

\begin{array}[]{rcl}\phi(1)&\overset{\text{def}}{=}&\text{smallest element of }X\text{ with respect to }\preceq\\
\phi(2)&\overset{\text{def}}{=}&\text{second smallest element of }X\text{ with respect to }\preceq\\
&\vdots&\\
\phi(N-1)&\overset{\text{def}}{=}&\text{second largest element of }X\text{ with respect to }\preceq\\
\phi(N)&\overset{\text{def}}{=}&\text{largest element of }X\text{ with respect to }\preceq\end{array}

Given this equivalence, elsewhere in the review there will in general be no explicit distinction made between a total order on a finite set and a bijection between that set and the index set corresponding to its cardinality. In particular, given a multi-index set
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\overset{\text{def}}{=}\bigtimes_{o=1}^{O}[M_{o}]
, a total order on
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
can equivalently be characterized via a choice of bijection
[M_{1}\dots M_{o}\dots M_{O}]\to[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
.

A.3.2
Equivalent Characterizations of Permutations of Finite Sets

There are two equivalent ways of thinking of permutations of a finite set
X
: (1) as orderings of the set
X
, i.e. bijections
[N]\xrightarrow{\phi}X
(where
|X|=N
), or (2) as (when
X
already has a specified ordering) re-orderings of the set
X
, i.e. (self-)bijections
X\xrightarrow{\pi}X
.

The elements of the set
X
can be interpreted as “labels”, and the elements of the set
[N]
can be thought of as “rankings”. So a bijection
[N]\xrightarrow{\phi}X
can be interpreted as a way of assigning each ranking (i.e. position) a unique label, such that each label is also assigned a unique ranking.

One often sees the notation e.g. of the form
(312)
for the permutation of the elements of a
3
-element set. This can be interpreted as specifying a bijection
[3]\xrightarrow{\phi}X
which specifies that the ranking of one, i.e. the first position, belongs to the element of the set
X
with label “
3
”, the ranking two belongs to the element of the set
X
with label “
1
”, and the ranking three belongs to the element of the set
X
with label “
2
”. (In other words, it
does
not say the opposite, e.g. that the element of the set
X
with label
1
gets sent to position
3
; in this case that element actually gets sent to position
2
,
not
position
3
.) The above notation for a permutation can also be interpreted as specifying a (self-)bijection
[3]\xrightarrow{\pi}[3]
such that
\pi(1)=3
,
\pi(2)=1
,
\pi(3)=2
.

Again, above
\pi(o_{1})=o_{2}
says that (after the permutation) the
o_{1}
’th position now belongs to
o_{2}
, and it does
not
say that the position of
o_{1}
after the permutation is
o_{2}
(which would be the opposite statement, i.e. correspond to
\pi^{-1}
). In other words, this review uses the convention that permutations, in both of their equivalent formulations, are specified via bijections:

\text{rankings}\quad\longrightarrow\quad\text{labels}\,,

even though it is also possible to specify orderings using the inverse functions
{\text{labels}\to\text{rankings}}
.

Given a specified ordering
[N]\xrightarrow{\psi}X
of the finite set
X
, e.g. the elements of
X
have been named such that
x_{1}\overset{\text{def}}{=}\psi(1)
, …,
x_{N}\overset{\text{def}}{=}\psi(N)
, one would like to consider how to re-arrange the elements of
X
so that they have the ordering corresponding to the bijection
[N]\xrightarrow{\pi}X
. In other words, given an element
x\in X
, which has rank/position
\psi^{-1}(x)
under the old ordering, one wants to know which element has that position under the new ordering,
\phi(\psi^{-1}(x))=(\phi\circ\psi^{-1})(x)
. In other words, the new ordering
[N]\xrightarrow{\phi}X
corresponds to the (self-)bijection
\phi\circ\psi^{-1}
of
X
:

X\xrightarrow{\pi}X\overset{\text{def}}{=}X\xrightarrow{\psi^{-1}}[N]\xrightarrow{\phi}X\,.

Conversely, starting with a self-bijection
X\xrightarrow{\pi}X
, and some specified (“standard”) ordering of
X
specified via the bijection
[N]\xrightarrow{\psi}X
, one gets a new ordering
\phi
of
X
via the rule:

[N]\xrightarrow{\phi}X\overset{\text{def}}{=}[N]\xrightarrow{\psi}X\xrightarrow{\pi}X\,.

In other words, if the element
x
is in the
n
’th position under the old order (
\psi(n)=x
), after the re-ordering specified by
\pi
, the element
\pi(x)
is now in the
n
’th position, i.e.
\phi(n)=\pi(x)
.

Thus these two distinct ways of thinking about permutations can be seen to be equivalent, since (given a “standard ordering” on the set
X
) one permutation of the first type specifies a unique permutation of the second type, and vice versa. According to
[
35
]
, the more straightforward interpretation as
91
91

91

Technically this is being sloppy and implicitly using the identification of orderings of
X
with bijections
[N]\to X
described in section
A.3.1
above. Strictly speaking the elementary interpretation corresponds to total orders of
X
.
bijections
[N]\to X
is older (and can be referred to for the sake of unambiguity as “passive permutations”), while the more abstract and modern interpretation as bijections
X\to X
used to be referred to as “substitutions” (and can be referred to for the sake of unambiguity as “active permutations”). Of course, in the case that the finite set
X
is itself an index set
[N]
there is mathematically speaking no distinction between the two. Since that is the most common scenario occurring in this review (usually the index set is the mode index set), no explicit distinction will be made between “passive permutations” and “active permutations” in this review. (The “standard ordering” in this case can be assumed to be the identity
{[N]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Id}_{[N]}}[N]}
.)

A.3.3
Lexicographical and Colexicographical Order

Given a multi-index set
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=\bigtimes_{o=1}^{O}[M_{o}]
, for each
o\in[O]
the corresponding mode
[M_{o}]
has a canonical order, namely the numerical order of the first
M_{o}
integers
1,2,\dots,M_{o}
. Given
O
totally ordered sets, there is a standard partial order
\preceq
defined on their Cartesian product, called the
product order
. For the multi-index set
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
, the product order
\preceq
amounts to the following:

\forall m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}},n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\in[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,\quad m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\preceq n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\iff m_{1}\leq n_{1}\,,m_{2}\leq n_{2}\,,\dots\,,m_{o}\leq n_{o}\,,\dots\,,m_{O}\leq n_{O}\,.

This is not a total order unless
O=1
because it leaves many, and usually most, pairs of multi-indices incomparable. For example, when
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[2]\times[2]
, it is neither the case that
(1,2)\preceq(2,1)
nor the case that
(2,1)\preceq(1,2)
. All that can be said is that with respect to the product order
\preceq
, there is no way to compare
(1,2)
and
(2,1)
. Thus more needs to be done to find a total order.

A total order
\leq
is said to be a
linear extension
92
92

92

This definition generalizes to the linear extension of any partial order, and the name comes from the fact that an alternative name for total order is linear order, since the numbers on the number line are totally ordered.
of the product order
\preceq
if
\leq
is compatible with
\preceq
in the sense that
m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\preceq n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}

always
implies that
m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\leq n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}
. Of course the converse,
m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\leq n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}
implies
m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\preceq n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{553683}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{481937}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{481932}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O]\mathstrut$}}}}}}
, is usually false, since again the partial order leaves most pairs of multi-indices incomparable. Thus the task of a linear extension is to compare those pairs left untouched by the product order
\preceq
in a way that preserves transitivity (
a\leq b
and
b\leq c
implies
a\leq c
).

The requirement that the total order for the multi-index set be a linear extension of the product order is a sensible one, since any order in which, for example, the following was possible:

(2081,496,1287)<(1,2,3)\,,

would seem and feel bizarre to most people. However, for most multi-index sets it still leaves far too many options available. For instance, for multi-index sets of the form either
[2]\times[M]
or
[M]\times[2]
with
M\geq 2
, the number of linear extensions of the product order is equal to the
M
’th Catalan number, which grows super-exponentially with
M
. The number is of course even higher for multi-index sets with either a larger number of modes or modes of greater sizes.

Thus to limit the options available to a reasonable amount, a second restriction on the total order can be imposed, namely that it be defined via a process

(1,1)<(1,2)<(2,1)<(2,2)\quad\text{and}\quad(1,1)<(2,1)<(1,2)<(2,2)\,.

Appendix A.4
The Categories of Multi-Index Sets

Explicitly defining categories is helpful for identifying the specific mathematical structure of interest. Working generally with the category of (unstructured) multi-index sets, or in special cases with the categories of structured multi-index sets, enables one to identify those issues in tensor algebra which are inherently combinatorial in nature and isolate them. The tensor shape functor then enables the transfer of combinatorial observations from the multi-index categories back to tensors, where they can subsequently be composed with algebraic observations.

A.4.1
The (Unfactorized) Category of Multi-Index Sets

The category of multi-index sets
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
is a
full subcategory

For example, the category of real vector spaces $“mathsf –Vect˝˙“R $ is “textit –not˝ a full subcategory of the category of sets $“sets $, because the morphisms between vector spaces are restricted to be linear functions in the category of real vector spaces $“mathsf –Vect˝˙“R $, whereas in the parent category of sets $“sets $ all possible arbitrary set functions between any two vector spaces are also present. all
multi-index sets, i.e. all finite sets of the form:

[M_{1}]\times[M_{2}]\times[M_{3}]\times\dots\times[M_{O}]\,,\quad\quad O,M_{1},M_{2},\dots,M_{O}\in\mathbb{N}\,,

and the morphisms of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
are
all
functions between multi-index sets.

A.4.2
Cartesian Product in the Category of Multi-Index Sets

The Cartesian product defines a functor
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}\times\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}\to\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.

A.4.2.1
Definition of the Cartesian Product on Objects

The product operation defined for
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
is different from the Cartesian product construction that is typically the product in subcategories of
\mathsf{Set}
. The idea is to exploit the highly specific structure of multi-index sets to define a modification of the typical Cartesian product which:

•

is associative up to equality, instead of only being associative up to isomorphism,

•

still satisfies the universal property of the (categorical) product,

•

returns another multi-index as output when given two multi-index as input.

For conceptual simplicity, since both product operations lead to sets which are uniquely isomorphic to each other in
\mathsf{Fin}\mathsf{Set}
and
\mathsf{Set}
95
95

95

Note that it would not be correct to say that they are also isomorphic in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
, even though it is a full subcategory of
\mathsf{Fin}\mathsf{Set}
, since the typical Cartesian product of two multi-index sets is usually not even an object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.
, and they correspond to functors which are naturally equivalent
96
96

96

For insight about why the distinct products are nevertheless naturally equivalent functors, compare the discussion in
A.10.1
. Here the universal property satisfied by both functors is the universal property of the (categorical) product.
, and since many might not even notice the distinction at all without it being pointed to them explicitly, the modified product operation in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
will also be referred to as the
Cartesian product
, even though it is distinct from the construction which is more typically called “Cartesian product”.

Given two objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
(where below
\bigtimes
refers to the Cartesian product of
\mathsf{Set}
):

[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=\bigtimes_{o=1}^{O_{1}}[M_{o}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,\quad[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=\bigtimes_{o=1}^{O_{2}}[M_{o}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,

their product
\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}
in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
is defined to be the set:

[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\overset{\text{def}}{=}\bigtimes_{o=1}^{O_{1}+O_{2}}[M_{o}]\,,\quad M_{o}=\begin{cases}M_{o}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}&\text{when }1\leq o\leq O_{1}\\
M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{o-O_{1}}&\text{when }O_{1}+1\leq o\leq O_{1}+O_{2}\end{cases}\,.

For example, if
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[2]\times[2]
, and
[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[2]
, then one has that:

\begin{array}[]{rcl}[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]&=&[2]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[2]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[2]\\
&=&\{(1,1,1),(1,1,2),(1,2,1),(1,2,2),\\
&&\phantom{\ \ }(2,1,1),(2,1,2),(2,2,1),(2,2,2)\}\,.\end{array}

Note the single level of parentheses, as well as that this is a multi-index set. In contrast:

\begin{array}[]{rcl}[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]&=&([2]\times[2])\times[2]\\
&=&\{((1,1),1),((1,1),2),((1,2),1),((1,2),2),\\
&&\phantom{\ \ }((2,1),1),((2,1),2),((2,2),1),((2,2),2)\}\,.\end{array}

Note the two levels of parentheses, and that this is not a Cartesian product of three index sets, but a Cartesian product of one multi-index set and one index set, and thus not a multi-index set itself.

Observe that by design these two constructions coincide for index sets:

[M]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[N]=[M]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[N]\,,\quad\forall M,N\in\mathbb{N}\,.

Observe also that the product in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
is associative up to equality, whereas the typical Cartesian product is only associative up to isomorphism. For example, for
\times_{\mathsf{Set}}
one has that:

\begin{array}[]{rcl}([2]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[2])\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[2]&=&\{((1,1),1),((1,1),2),((1,2),1),((1,2),2),\\
&&\phantom{\ \ }((2,1),1),((2,1),2),((2,2),1),((2,2),2)\}\\
&\not=&\{(1,(1,1)),(1,(1,2)),(1,(2,1)),(1,(2,2)),\\
&&\phantom{\ \ }(2,(1,1)),(2,(1,2)),(2,(2,1)),(2,(2,2))\}\\
&=&[2]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}([2]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[2])\,.\end{array}

Even though there is an obvious bijection between the two sets above, such that they are isomorphic, they are nevertheless not equal. In contrast, for
\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}
one has that:

([2]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[2])\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[2]=[2]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[2]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[2]=[2]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}([2]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[2])\,,

where by definition
[2]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[2]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[2]=[2]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[2]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[2]
. No isomorphisms are required to identify any of the three sets, instead all three of them are already equal.

More generally, one only has for the Cartesian product in
\mathsf{Set}
that:

\begin{array}[]{rcccl}(X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y)\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Z&\not=&X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Z&\not=&X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(Y\times_{\mathsf{Set}})Z\,,\\
(X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y)\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Z&\cong_{\mathsf{Set}}&X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Z&\cong_{\mathsf{Set}}&X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(Y\times_{\mathsf{Set}})Z\,,\end{array}

since for arbitrary elements
x\in X
,
y\in Y
,
z\in Z
, elements of
(X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y)\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Z
are of the form
((x,y),z)
, elements of
X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Z
are of the form
(x,y,z)
, and elements of
X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(Y\times_{\mathsf{Set}})Z
are of the form
(x,(y,z))
, none of which are equal. Here
\cong_{\mathsf{Set}}
means equivalent up to isomorphism in the category
\mathsf{Set}
, i.e. that there exists a bijection between the sets
97
97

97

The relation
\cong_{\mathsf{Set}}
of equivalence up to isomorphism is a transitive relation, while technically
\not=
is not. Nevertheless it also true that
(X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y)\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Z\not=X\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(Y\times_{\mathsf{Set}})Z
, even if it did not say so explicitly above.
.

In contrast, for the product operation
\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}
in the category
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
, one has that:

([M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}])\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[P_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[P_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}([N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[P_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaysty for
all
multi-index sets
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
,
[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
, and
[P_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
. This is associativity up to equality.

For two given multi-index sets
{[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=\bigtimes_{o=1}^{O_{1}}[M_{o}]}
and
{[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=\bigtimes_{o=1}^{O_{2}}[N_{o}]}
, there always exists a canonical
98
98

98

It is unique among all bijections in transforming the projection maps of one set to the projection maps of the other, i.e. in being compatible with the universal property of the product satisfied by both sets.
bijection
\phi:[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
. Here is its rule of assignment:

\begin{array}[]{rlcrl}&(m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}},n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}})=&&&\\
\phi:&((m_{1},\dotsc,m_{O_{1}}),(n_{1},\dotsc,n_{O_{2}}))&\mapsto&(m_{1},\dotsc,m_{O_{1}},n_{1},\dotsc,n_{O_{2}})&\overset{\text{def}}{=}\\
&&&m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}&\overset{\text{def}}{=}\\
&&&m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}n_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\,.&\end{array}

For example, taking
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[2]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[2]\times[2]
and
[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[1]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[2]
as in the example above, one has that:

\phi:((1,1),2)\mapsto(1,1,2)\,,\quad\phi:((2,2),1))\mapsto(2,2,1)\,,\quad\phi:((1,2),1)\mapsto(1,2,1)\,,\quad\text{etc.}

This definition of product in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
also makes the definition of the Segre outer product
\otimes
much less unwieldy compared to a comparable definition using the tensor product of functions
\otimes_{func}
defined in section
3
. In particular, one has for tensors
\mathbfcal{T}:[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{552122}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{608292}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to\mathbb{R}
and
\mathbfcal{U}:[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{552122}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{608292}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to\mathbb{R}
that:

\mathbfcal{T}\otimes\mathbfcal{U}\overset{\text{def}}{=}(\mathbfcal{T}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U})\circ\phi^{-1}\,,

since, comparing domains and codomains, one sees that:

\mathbfcal{T}\otimes\mathbfcal{U}:[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{552122}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{608292}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{552122}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{608292}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to\mathbb{R}\,,\quad\mathbfcal{T}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U}:[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{552122}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{608292}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{601863}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.16666pt}{\resizebox{552122}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{608292}{229376}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to\mathbb{R}\,.

One example of why this is useful is because it allows one to say for any three tensors
\mathbfcal{S},\mathbfcal{T},\mathbfcal{U}
:

{(\mathbfcal{S}\otimes\mathbfcal{T})\otimes\mathbfcal{U}}=\mathbfcal{S}\otimes\mathbfcal{T}\otimes\mathbfcal{U}=\mathbfcal{S}\otimes(\mathbfcal{T}\otimes\mathbfcal{U})\,,

i.e. that all three tensors are the same up to
equality
, not merely up to isomorphism
99
99

99

Which strictly speaking is all one can do using the typical tensor product construction found e.g. in Chapter 2 of
[
14
]
.
. However, the analogous statement would be false using the definition
\otimes_{func}
: the three functions
{(\mathbfcal{S}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{T})\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U}}
,
{\mathbfcal{S}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{T}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U}}
, and
\mathbfcal{S}\otimes_{func}(\mathbfcal{T}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U})
don’t even have the same domain and therefore certainly aren’t equal. Moreover, in general
none
of the functions
{(\mathbfcal{S}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{T})\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U}}
,
{\mathbfcal{S}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{T}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U}}
, and
\mathbfcal{S}\otimes_{func}(\mathbfcal{T}\otimes_{func}\mathbfcal{U})
are tensors, since their domains are not multi-index sets, only Cartesian products of multi-index sets. Thus the definition for the product in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
ensures that the Segre outer product returns a tensor as output when given tensors as input.

Throughout this review, whenever
\bigtimes
or
\times
is written to denote some product of multi-index sets, one can safely assume that the product in question is the product operation
\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}
and not
\times_{\mathsf{Set}}
.

A.4.2.2
Definition of the Cartesian Product on Morphisms

One has the same issues for functions that one has for sets with
\times_{\mathsf{Set}}
. Specifically, given functions:

f_{1}:X_{1}\to Y_{1}\,,\quad f_{2}:X_{2}\to Y_{2}\,,\quad f_{3}:X_{3}\to Y_{3}\,,

none of the following three functions are equal:

\begin{array}[]{rccl}(f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2})\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{3}:&(X_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}X_{2})\times_{\mathsf{Set}}X_{3}&\to&(Y_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y_{2})\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y_{3}\,,\\
f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{3}:&X_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}X_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}X_{3}&\to&Y_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y_{3}\,,\\
f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(f_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{3}):&X_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(X_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}X_{3})&\to&Y_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(Y_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}Y_{3})\,.\end{array}

This is clearly true since none of their domains are the same, and none of their codomains are the same. They all take different types of inputs and return different types of outputs:

\begin{array}[]{rccl}(f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2})\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{3}:&((x_{1},x_{2}),x_{3})&\mapsto&((f_{1}(x_{1}),f_{2}(x_{2})),f_{3}(x_{3}))\,,\\
f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{3}:&(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})&\mapsto&(f_{1}(x_{1}),f_{2}(x_{2}),f_{3}(x_{3}))\,,\\
f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}(f_{2}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{3}):&(x_{1},(x_{2},x_{3}))&\mapsto&(f_{1}(x_{1}),(f_{2}(x_{2}),f_{3}(x_{3})))\,.\end{array}

To avoid problems like this, the Cartesian product of functions in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
is defined differently. (It needs to be defined differently in any case, since the Cartesian product in
\mathsf{Set}
of two functions
f_{1}:[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[N^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{669657}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{735411}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
and
f_{2}:[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[N^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{669657}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{735411}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
is the function:

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[N^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{669657}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{735411}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[N^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{669657}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{735411}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,

for which neither the domain nor codomain are multi-index sets in general. Moreover, the Cartesian product functor in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
applied to the domains of
f_{1}
and
