, then one has:

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}\overset{\text{def}}{=}\psi\circ(f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2})\circ\phi^{-1}\,.

The bijections
\phi,\psi
basically “remove parentheses”, and the bijections
\phi^{-1},\psi^{-1}
“add parentheses”.

Note that this definition of Cartesian product, in addition to being the “correct choice” by virtue of being the morphism induced by the universal property of the product, also has the virtue of being associative up to equality, not just isomorphism. In other words, given any morphisms of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
:

f_{1}:[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[N^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{669657}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{735411}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,\quad f_{2}:[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[N^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{669657}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{735411}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,\quad f_{3}:[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[N^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(3)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{727886}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{669657}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{735411}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D_{3}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,

one always has the following relationships:

(f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2})\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{3}=f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{3}=f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}(f_{2}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{3})\,.

Therefore the order and number of parentheses do not affect the result.

For an example of the definition of Cartesian product for functions in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
, consider

f_{1}:[4]\to[2]\times[2]\,,\quad f_{1}(1)=(1,1)\,,f_{1}(2)=(2,1)\,,f_{1}(3)=(1,2)\,,f_{1}(4)=(2,2)\,,

and

f_{2}:[2]\times[2]\to[4]\,,\quad f_{2}(1,1)=1\,,f_{2}(1,2)=2\,,f_{2}(2,1)=3\,,f_{2}(2,2)=4\,.

Then for the values of the Cartesian product function of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
:

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:[4]\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}([2]\times[2])=[4]\times[2]\times[2]\to[2]\times[2]\times[4]=([2]\times[2])\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}[4]

one has the following:

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(1,1,1)

\mapsto

(1,1,1)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(1,1,2)

\mapsto

(1,1,2)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(1,2,1)

\mapsto

(1,1,3)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(1,2,2)

\mapsto

(1,1,4)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(2,1,1)

\mapsto

(2,1,1)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(2,1,2)

\mapsto

(2,1,2)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(2,2,1)

\mapsto

(2,1,3)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(2,2,2)

\mapsto

(2,1,4)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(3,1,1)

\mapsto

(1,2,1)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(3,1,2)

\mapsto

(1,2,2)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(3,2,1)

\mapsto

(1,2,3)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(3,2,2)

\mapsto

(1,2,4)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(4,1,1)

\mapsto

(2,2,1)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(4,1,2)

\mapsto

(2,2,2)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(4,2,1)

\mapsto

(2,2,3)

f_{1}\times_{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}f_{2}:(4,2,2)

\mapsto

(2,2,4)\,.

In contrast, for the values of the Cartesian product function of
\mathsf{Set}
:

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:[4]\times_{\mathsf{Set}}([2]\times[2])\to([2]\times[2])\times_{\mathsf{Set}}[4]\,,

one has the following instead:

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(1,(1,1))

\mapsto

((1,1),1)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(1,(1,2))

\mapsto

((1,1),2)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(1,(2,1))

\mapsto

((1,1),3)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(1,(2,2))

\mapsto

((1,1),4)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(2,(1,1))

\mapsto

((2,1),1)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(2,(1,2))

\mapsto

((2,1),2)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(2,(2,1))

\mapsto

((2,1),3)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(2,(2,2))

\mapsto

((2,1),4)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(3,(1,1))

\mapsto

((1,2),1)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(3,(1,2))

\mapsto

((1,2),2)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(3,(2,1))

\mapsto

((1,2),3)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(3,(2,2))

\mapsto

((1,2),4)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(4,(1,1))

\mapsto

((2,2),1)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(4,(1,2))

\mapsto

((2,2),2)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(4,(2,1))

\mapsto

((2,2),3)

f_{1}\times_{\mathsf{Set}}f_{2}:(4,(2,2))

\mapsto

((2,2),4)\,.

Clearly these functions are very similar, and in fact they are related via canonical bijections induced by the universal property of the product, but only the first one is a morphism in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.

A.4.3
The
D
-Factorized Categories of Multi-Index Sets

The definition of the
D
-factorized categories of multi-index sets
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
initially requires some explanation, but becomes straightforward to understand after thinking through some examples.

A.4.3.1
Objects of the
D
-Factorized Category of Multi-Index Sets

For a given
D\geq 1
, the objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
each consist of two data: (i) a multi-index set with
O\geq D
modes, and (ii) a chosen
contiguous
101
101

101

As explained elsewhere, only considering contiguous partitions does not actually come with any loss of generality, due to the possibility of permuting modes beforehand to ensure that one’s desired partition becomes contiguous.
partition of those
O
modes into
D
blocks.

For an example of what this means, consider the
2
-factorized category of multi-index sets,
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
. Then for the following multi-index set with
3\geq 2
modes:

[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\overset{\text{def}}{=}[7]\times[5]\times[14]

there are
\binom{3-1}{2-1}=\binom{2}{1}=2
objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
associated with it, since
\binom{O-1}{D-1}
counts the number of distinct ways to partition a set with
O
elements into
D
contiguous blocks.

Specifically, the two objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
associated with
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=[7]\times[5]\times[4]
are:

[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}\overset{\text{def}}{=}([7]\times[5]\times[14],\{\{1,2\},\{3\}\}),\quad[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|23}\overset{\text{def}}{=}([7]\times[5]\times[14],\{\{1\},\{2,3\}\})\,.

In contrast, given a multi-index set with
2
modes, there is exactly
\binom{2-1}{1-1}=\binom{1}{0}=1
object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
which is associated with it. For instance, the multi-index set:

[23]\times[17]

is associated uniquely with the following object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
:

([23]\times[17],\{\{1\},\{2\}\})\,.

The objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
can be thought of as consisting of two distinct strata: (i) all multi-index sets with exactly
D
modes, which are endowed with no extra structure, and (ii) multi-index sets with
O>D
modes endowed with a given contiguous partition of their
O
modes into
D
blocks (with the result that each such multi-index set is associated with
\binom{O-1}{D-1}
distinct objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
).

The idea is that the objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
should have “
D
-fold Cartesian product structure”.

While there is clearly only one way that a multi-index set with exactly
D
modes can be considered to have such
D
-fold Cartesian product structure, for multi-index sets with
O>D
modes one needs to be specific about how the multi-index set is being considered as having
D
-fold Cartesian product structure, since there are
\binom{O-1}{D-1}
distinct possible groupings of the
O
modes which would enable such an interpretation, each corresponding to a different contiguous partition of
[O]
.

Also notice that, since for every
O\geq 1
there is exactly
\binom{O-1}{1-1}=\binom{O-1}{0}=1
way to partition
O
modes into one block
102
102

102

Since there is only one block, the restriction that the partition be contiguous is redundant.
, the objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{1}
are essentially the same as those of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.

A.4.3.2
Morphisms of the
D
-Factorized Category of Multi-Index Sets

Given two objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
, the morphisms between them consist of all
D
-fold Cartesian products of functions between their
D
corresponding blocks of modes.

For an example of what this definition means when
D=2
, consider the objects
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}
and
[23]\times[17]
of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
. Given any two functions (equivalently morphisms in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
):

f_{1}:[7]\times[5]\to[23]\,,\quad f_{2}:[14]\to[17]\,,

then the Cartesian product of those two functions:

f_{1}\times f_{2}:[7]\times[5]\times[14]\to[23]\times[17]

is a morphism in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}
to
[23]\times[17]
.

Conversely, by definition
every
morphism in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
starting from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}
and going to
[23]\times[17]
is of the form
f_{1}\times f_{2}
for some functions
f_{1}:[7]\times[5]\to[23]
and
f_{2}:[14]\to[17]
.

Similarly, the morphisms in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
starting from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|23}
(note the different partition) and going to
[23]\times[17]
are the set of all functions which are of the form:

g_{1}\times g_{2}:[7]\times[5]\times[14]\to[23]\times[17]\,,

for
any
functions
g_{1}
and
g_{2}
such that:

g_{1}:[7]\to[23]\,,\quad g_{2}:[5]\times[14]\to[17]\,.

The idea is that the morphisms in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
should preserve the specified
D
-fold Cartesian product structures of their domain and codomain, and thus have
D
-fold Cartesian product structure as well.

Note that for functions
g_{1}:[7]\to[23]
and
g_{2}:[5]\times[14]\to[17]
, the function
g_{1}\times g_{2}
is
not
a morphism in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}
to
[23]\times[17]
, even though the function is a morphism from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|23}
to
[23]\times[17]
in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
, as well as a morphism from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
to
[23]\times[17]
in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.

Similarly, for functions
f_{1}:[7]\times[5]\to[23]
and
f_{2}:[14]\to[17]
, the function
f_{1}\times f_{2}
is
not
a morphism in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|23}
to
[23]\times[17]
, even though the function is a morphism from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}
to
[23]\times[17]
in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
, as well as a morphism from
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
to
[23]\times[17]
in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.

Thus the principal effect of attaching the extra structure of a partition of modes to the objects in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
is to limit the number of functions between those objects which are considered valid morphisms. Moreover, when different partitions of modes into
D
blocks are attached to the same multi-index set, the answer to which functions are valid morphisms in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
changes.

Also notice that, since the
1
-fold Cartesian product of a function
f
is just the function
f
itself, the morphisms of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{1}
are essentially the same as those of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.

A.4.3.3
Remarks about the
D
-Factorized Categories of Multi-Index Sets

Since both the objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{1}
and the morphisms of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{1}
are essentially the same as their counterparts in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
, the two categories
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{1}
and
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
are for all intents and purposes the same category. Therefore, from now on
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{1}
will be redefined so that
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{1}=\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
.

Notice that for any
O>D
, the objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
which are associated with the objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{O}
(namely those multi-index sets with
O
or more modes) are a strict subset of the objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
which are associated with objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
(those multi-index sets with
D
or more modes).

Moreover, for
O>D
, one can define
\binom{O-1}{D-1}
distinct forgetful functors from
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{O}
to
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
. I.e. there are
\binom{O-1}{D-1}
distinct ways for a multi-index set to “forget” its
O
-fold Cartesian product structure, and to remember only a coarser
D
-fold Cartesian product structure instead. Each given contiguous partition of
[O]
into
D
blocks provides a pattern for merging the
O
blocks of modes of the objects in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{O}
into
D
blocks of modes, and thus selects associated objects of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
.

For example, there are
\binom{3-1}{2-1}=2
distinct forgetful functors from
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{3}
to
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
.

The first such functor, denoted
\mathscr{F}_{1|23}
, corresponding to the contiguous partition
\{\{1\},\{2,3\}\}
, allows an object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{3}
to remember its first block of modes, but makes that object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{3}
forget that its second and third blocks of modes were distinct and thus merges them into one block of modes. Here are some examples of the behavior of
\mathscr{F}_{1|23}
, where
[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\overset{\text{def}}{=}[5]\times[37]\times[29]\times[41]
:

\begin{array}[]{lcl}\mathscr{F}_{1|23}([M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}])&=&[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|23}\\
\mathscr{F}_{1|23}([N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3|4})&=&[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|34}\\
\end{array}

The second such functor, denoted
\mathscr{F}_{12|3}
, corresponding to the contiguous partition
\{\{1,2\},\{3\}\}
, makes an object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{3}
forget that its first and second of modes were distinct and thus merges them into one block of modes, but allows that object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{3}
to remember its third block of modes. Here are some examples of the behavior of
\mathscr{F}_{12|3}

\begin{array}[]{lcl}\mathscr{F}_{12|3}([M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|2|3})&=&[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}\\
\mathscr{F}_{12|3}([N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3|4})&=&[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{123|4}\\

\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{O}

[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{P_{2}}

from

\mathscr{F}_{Q}([M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{P_{1}})=[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{P_{1}\blacktriangleright Q}

\mathscr{F}_{1|23}:\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{3}\to\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
:

\mathscr{F}_{1|23}([M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|2|3})=[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|23}\quad\to\quad[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|34}=\mathscr{F}_{1|23}([N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3|4})\,.

However, the converse is false. In other words, there will always be morphisms in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
from
\mathscr{F}_{Q}([M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{P_{1}})
to
\mathscr{F}_{Q}([M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{P_{2}})
which do not preserve
O
-fold Cartesian product structure, i.e. which are not morphisms in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{O}
from
[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{1}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{P_{1}}
to
[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{732950}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{640458}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{704563}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{646335}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63889pt}{\resizebox{712089}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{2}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{P_{2}}
. Such morphisms in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
are not the image of any morphism in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{O}
under any forgetful functor
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{O}\to\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
. Thus the image of any of these forgetful functors always fails to be a full subcategory of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
.

As an example, while the function

f=f_{1}\times f_{2}:[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\to[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]\,,

where the functions
f_{1}
and
f_{2}
have the following domains and codomains:

f_{1}:[7]\times[5]\to[5]\times[37]\times[29]\,,\quad f_{2}:[14]\to[41]\,,

is
a morphism in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{2}
:

\mathscr{F}_{12|3}([M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}])=[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3}\quad\to\quad[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{123|4}=\mathscr{F}_{12|3}([N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3|4})\,,

in general it is
not
a morphism:

[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[3]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{1|2|3}\quad\to\quad[N_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{435452}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{377912}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{377909}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[4]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]_{12|3|4}

in
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{3}
(except whenever
f_{1}=h_{1}\times h_{2}
for some
h_{1}:[7]\to[5]\times[37]
and
h_{2}:[5]\to[29]
).

Note finally that, for each
D\geq 1
, the category
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
is equivalent to the image of the
D
-fold Cartesian product functor defined above for the category
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}
in section
A.4.2
:

\bigtimes_{d=1}^{D}\underbrace{\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}\times\cdots\times\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}}_{D\text{ times}}\to\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}\,.

In other words, every object of
\bm{\mathsf{MltIdx}}_{D}
has isomorphic
D
-fold Cartesian product structure to some object
\bigtimes_{d=1}^{D}[M^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{745605}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(d)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{745605}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(d)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{650727}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(d)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{650727}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(d)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{709697}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[O_{d}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{709697}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[O_{d}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{651574}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[O_{d}]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{719423}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[O_{d}]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]
in the image of the
D
-fold Cartesian product functor.

Appendix A.5
Identification of
\mathbb{R}^{L}
with
\mathbb{R}^{[L]}

It can be verified for each
\ell\in[L]
, the projection functions
\pi_{\ell}:\mathbb{R}^{[L]}\to\mathbb{R}
given by
\mathbf{v}\mapsto\mathbf{v}(\ell)\overset{\text{def}}{=}v_{\ell}
are linear, and that
\mathbb{R}^{[L]}
together with the
L
projection functions
\pi_{\ell}
satisfy the universal property of the
L
-fold product for
\mathbb{R}
in the category of finite-dimensional real vector spaces.

One may also verify that the
L
-fold Cartesian product of copies of
\mathbb{R}
,
\bigtimes_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbb{R}
, whose elements correspond to ordered lists, or tuples, of real numbers of length
L
,
(v_{1},\dots,v_{\ell},\dots,v_{L})
, is also a real vector space, and that
\bigtimes_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbb{R}
together with the
L
linear projection functions
p_{\ell}:\bigtimes_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}
(which, given such a tuple
(v_{1},\dots,v_{\ell},\dots,v_{L})
return the
\ell
’th element
v_{\ell}
) also satisfy the universal property of the
L
-fold product of
\mathbb{R}
in the category of finite-dimensional real vector spaces.

Therefore, there is a
canonical
linear isomorphism
104
104

104

It is the unique isomorphism compatible with the specified projection functions
\pi_{\ell}
and
p_{\ell}
.
between
\mathbb{R}^{[L]}
and
\bigtimes_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbb{R}
, such that they are “essentially the same” real vector space. In light of this, in what follows
\mathbb{R}^{[L]}
and
\bigtimes_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbb{R}
will generally not be distinguished between explicitly. Instead the notation
105
105

105

Which is more commonly reserved for
\bigtimes_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbb{R}
only.

\mathbb{R}^{L}
will be used to denote both spaces and the notation
(v_{1},\dots,v_{\ell},\dots,v_{L})
to denote elements of either space.

Appendix A.6
Coordinate Isomorphisms

Every object
\mathbb{V}
in
\mathsf{Fin}_{\mathbb{R}}\mathsf{Vect}
is isomorphic as a vector space to
\mathbb{R}^{M}
for
M=\dim(V)
. Similarly, every object
\mathbb{T}
(with “tensor factors”
\mathbb{V}_{1}
,
\mathbb{V}_{2}
, …,
\mathbb{V}_{D}
) of
\mathsf{Fin}_{\mathbb{R}}\mathsf{Tens}_{D}
is isomorphic as a
D
-fold tensor space to
\mathbb{R}^{[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453877}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453878}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]}
where
[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{577006}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{577006}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36572pt}{\resizebox{505259}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.36574pt}{\resizebox{505254}{268516}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]=\bigtimes_{d=1}^{D}[M_{d}]
with
M_{d}=\dim(\mathbb{V}_{d})
for all
d\in\mathbb{V}_{d}
. Combining these two statements, one could reach the conclusion that (for finite-dimensional spaces with real scalars) all problems in linear algebra and all problems in multilinear algebra can be reduced to the study of coordinate spaces
\mathbb{R}^{[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453877}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453878}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]}
. This is the reason why such spaces are the focus of this review.

A.6.1
Coordinate Isomorphisms for Vector Spaces

Given a vector space
\mathbb{V}
with
\dim(\mathbb{V})=M
, choose some basis
\mathscr{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_{1},\dots,\mathbf{b}_{M}\}
, which then uniquely defines
M
linear functions in
\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{V};\mathbb{R})\overset{\text{def}}{=}\left(\mathbb{V}\right)^{\ast}
via the formulae:

\varphi_{m}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbf{b}_{\mu}\mapsto\delta_{m\mu}\,,

where
\delta_{m\mu}
denotes the Kronecker delta (
\delta_{m\mu}=1
if
m=\mu
and
0
otherwise). Then with respect to the chosen basis
\mathscr{B}
, any
\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{V}
may be written in the form:

\mathbf{v}=\varphi_{1}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})\mathbf{b}_{1}+\varphi_{2}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})\mathbf{b}_{2}+\dots+\varphi_{M}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})\mathbf{b}_{M}\,.

For any vector
\mathbf{v}\in V
the
M
linear functions
\varphi_{m}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}
give the scalar coefficients in the unique linear combination writing
\mathbf{v}
in terms of the elements of the basis
\mathscr{B}
. In other words, the
M
linear functions
\varphi_{m}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}
define, for every vector
\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{V}
, the coordinates of
\mathbf{v}
with respect to the basis
\mathscr{B}
.

For any chosen basis
\mathscr{B}
, one can verify that all of the coordinate functions
\varphi_{1}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}
together collectively form a basis for
\left(\mathbb{V}\right)^{\ast}
, denoted
\left(\mathscr{B}\right)^{\ast}
. The basis
\left(\mathscr{B}\right)^{\ast}
is called the
dual basis
of
\mathscr{B}
.

As an example, if
\mathbb{V}=\{a\sin(x)+b\sin(2x):a,b\in\mathbb{R}\}
, then for
\mathbf{v}=\sin(x)+\sin(2x)
, for

\mathscr{B}=\{\sin(x),\sin(2x)\}\,,

then the values of the coordinate functions are
\varphi_{1}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})=1
and
\varphi_{2}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})=1
, and for

\mathscr{C}=\left\{\frac{1}{2}\sin(x)+\frac{1}{2}\sin(2x),\frac{1}{2}\sin(x)-\frac{1}{2}\sin(2x)\right\}\,,

the values of the coordinate functions are
\varphi_{1}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{856268}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{856268}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{751843}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{751842}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})=2
and
\varphi_{2}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{856268}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{856268}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{751843}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{751842}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{C})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})=0
.

As another example, the dual basis corresponding to the standard basis of
\mathbb{R}^{L}
consists of the projection functions
\pi_{\ell}
or equivalently
p_{\ell}
defined in section
A.5
. For each
\ell\in[L]
, one has that
\varphi_{\ell}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{840357}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(L)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{840357}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(L)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{730957}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(L)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{730958}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(L)\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})=\pi_{\ell}(\mathbf{v})=v_{\ell}
, i.e. it just returns the
\ell
’th entry of the vector
\mathbf{v}
. It is also true for higher-order tensors that the dual basis of the standard basis is very simple, consisting of coordinate functions which return the corresponding entry of the tensor.

For any basis
\mathscr{B}
of any
M
-dimensional real vector space
\mathbb{V}
, the dual basis
\left(\mathscr{B}\right)^{\ast}
construction allows one to define an isomorphism identifying
\mathbb{V}
with
\mathbb{R}^{M}
:

\Phi^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbb{V}\to\mathbb{R}^{M}

called the
coordinate isomorphism
with respect to
\mathscr{B}
, using the rule of assignment:

\Phi^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbf{v}\mapsto\varphi_{1}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})\mathbf{e}_{1}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1047311}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1047311}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{930752}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{930751}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}}+\varphi_{2}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})\mathbf{e}_{2}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1047311}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1047311}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{930752}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{930751}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(M)\mathstrut$}}}}}}+\cdots+\varphi_{M}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v})\mathbf{e}_{M}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1047311}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle({M})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1047311}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle({M})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{930752}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle({M})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{930751}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle({M})\mathstrut$}}}}}}\,.

Therefore everything that can be said about
\mathbb{V}
as a finite-dimensional real vector space can be explored by choosing a basis for
\mathscr{B}
and subsequently working in the coordinate space
\mathbb{R}^{M}
.

Note further that one can exploit multilinearity such that for any elementary tensor:

\mathbfcal{T}=\mathbf{v}_{1}\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\mathbf{v}_{2}\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\cdots\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\mathbf{v}_{D}\,,

one has the following relationship:

\varphi_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453877}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453878}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbfcal{T})=\varphi_{m_{1}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{904675}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{904675}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{832912}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.95999pt}{\resizebox{911554}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v}_{1})\varphi_{m_{2}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{904675}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{2})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{904675}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{2})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{832912}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{2})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.95999pt}{\resizebox{911554}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscr and therefore:

\mathbfcal{T}=\sum_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\in[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]}\varphi_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{724233}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{724233}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{636304}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{636304}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbfcal{T})\mathbfcal{B}_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displays Thus, for
any
tensor
\mathbfcal{T}\in\mathbb{T}
, given any outer product decomposition of
\mathbfcal{T}
:

\mathbfcal{T}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbf{v}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569402}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569401}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{1}\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\mathbf{v}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569402}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569401}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{2}\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\cdots\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\mathbf{v}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569402}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569401}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{D}\,,

one has the relationship:

\varphi_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453877}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453878}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbfcal{T})=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\prod_{d=1}^{D}\varphi_{m_{d}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{910815}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{910815}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{839177}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.28664pt}{\resizebox{920326}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569402}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569401}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{d})\right)\,,

so that finally:

\mathbfcal{T}=\sum_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\in[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\prod_{d=1}^{D}\varphi_{m_{d}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{910815}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{910815}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{839177}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.28664pt}{\resizebox{920326}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{652660}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569402}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{569401}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{d})\right)\right)\mathbf{b}_{m_{1}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{626111}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{626111}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{547102}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{547102}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(1)\mathstrut$}}}}}}\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\mathbf{b}_{m_{2}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{626111}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{626111}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{547102}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{547102}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(2)\mathstrut$}}}}}}\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\cdots\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}\mathbf{b}_{m_{D}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{795399}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(D)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{795399}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(D)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{699399}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(D)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{699397}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(D)\mathstrut$}}}}}}\,.

The result does not depend on the particular outer product decomposition of
\mathbfcal{T}
chosen due to the universal property of the
D
-fold tensor product satisfied (by assumption) by
\mathbb{T}
using
\otimes_{\mathbb{T}}
.

Analogous to before, the existence of a dual basis
\left(B\right)^{\ast}
for the chosen basis
\mathscr{B}
of
\mathbb{T}
, which allows one to write the coordinates of any
\mathbfcal{T}\in\mathbb{T}
with respect to
\mathscr{B}
using the elements of
\left(B\right)^{\ast}
, also enables one to define a
D
-fold tensor space isomorphism:

\Phi^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbb{T}\to\mathbb{R}^{[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453877}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453878}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]}\,,

called again the
coordinate isomorphism
, via the rule of assignment:

\Phi^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{847815}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{744882}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbfcal{T}\mapsto\sum_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\in[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]}\varphi_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{426020}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.83333pt}{\resizebox{308290}{163840}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.63332pt}{\resizebox{724233}{321125}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mat where as usual

denotes the unit tensor (see section
2
) of

corresponding to the multi-index

Observe that this

is already completely determined by the
D
respective vector space coordinate isomorphisms defined in section
A.6.1

\Phi^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1059046}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1059046}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{975038}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.29443pt}{\resizebox{1067100}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.05pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{1})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbb{V}_{1}\to\mathbb{R}^{M_{1}}\,,\dots\,,\Phi^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1066234}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1066234}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{982373}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.67682pt}{\resizebox{1077368}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbb{V}_{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{M_{d}}\,,\dots,\,,\Phi^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1183845}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{D})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1183845}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{D})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{1102383}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{D})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.59186pt}{\resizebox{1245382}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.18611pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{D})\mathstrut$}}}}}}:\mathbb{V}_{D}\to\mathbb{R}^{M_{D}}\,,

since given any outer product decomposition of any tensor

&=&\displaystyle\sum_{m_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453877}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453878}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}\in[M_{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{627204}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453877}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.22687pt}{\resizebox{453878}{241212}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle[D]\mathstrut$}}}}}}]}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\prod_{d=1}^{D}\varphi_{m_{d}}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1066234}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{1066234}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{982373}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.67682pt}{\resizebox{1077368}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(\mathscr{B}_{d})\mathstrut$}}}}}}(\mathbf{v}^{\scriptsize\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{764028}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{764028}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91202pt}{\resizebox{666563}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.91203pt}{\resizebox{666563}{375921}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle(k)\mathstrut$}}}}}}_{d})\right)\right)\mathbfcal{I}_{m_
